prompt_text: What is the best AI video ad maker?
answer_verbatim:
There isn’t a single “best” AI video ad maker — the right tool depends on your goals (spokesperson vs. animated text, scale vs. one-off, budget, target platform). That said, these are the top options (strength, when to pick it, key downside):

- Synthesia
  - Strength: Very polished AI human presenters/avatars, multi‑language voice + script-to-video. Great for product demos, explainer ads where a “talking person” is needed.
  - Downside: Costlier than template tools; less flexible for flashy motion graphics.

- HeyGen (formerly Movio) / Replacements in that space
  - Strength: Competitive alternative to Synthesia — good avatars, faster turnaround and sometimes lower price.
  - Downside: Quality varies by avatar and language; still limited creative motion compared with full editors.

- Pictory
  - Strength: Text‑to‑video and long-form → short clip repurposing (great for turning blog posts, webinars into social ads).
  - Downside: Less control over fine motion/animation; templates can feel generic.

- Canva (Video) / InVideo
  - Strength: Best for marketers who want quick, editable templates, stock library, and captions — very fast for social ad assembly.
  - Downside: Not true “AI actor” features; more template-driven.

- Promo.com
  - Strength: Built specifically for ads — huge ad templates and licensed music/stock footage optimized for platforms (Facebook, Instagram, TikTok).
  - Downside: Template look can be similar across brands unless customized.

- Rephrase.ai / Idomi (personalization platforms)
  - Strength: Personalized video at scale (e.g., name or dynamic offers inserted per viewer) — great for performance marketing and CRM-driven campaigns.
  - Downside: Integration complexity and cost.

- Runway / Kaiber (generative/creative)
  - Strength: Cutting-edge generative visuals and effects for attention-grabbing creative.
  - Downside: Steeper learning curve and results can be experimental.

- Descript
  - Strength: Excellent for editing, captions, overdub voice cloning — nice when your ad is repurposed from recorded audio/video.
  - Downside: Not a template ad-maker; more of an editor.

How to choose quickly
- Want a human presenter or multilingual spokesperson? → Synthesia or HeyGen.
- Want to repurpose blog posts/webinars into short ads? → Pictory.
- Need fast, cheap social ads from templates with lots of stock assets? → Canva, InVideo, or Promo.com.
- Need personalized 1:1 ads at scale? → Rephrase.ai or similar.
- Want creative, experimental visuals? → Runway or Kaiber.

If you tell me: platform (Facebook/Instagram/YouTube/TikTok), style (spokesperson, text+stock, animated), budget (free/low/enterprise), and whether you need personalization or localization, I’ll recommend the single best option and a short workflow/template for making an ad.
session_note: run_channel caveat: API results can differ from logged-in consumer apps, no memory, no personalization.
